acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ Written BEFORE the code, unlike ACC-0001..0009. `not-evaluated` is the honest state and is exactly the distinction QST-0015 was about: the criterion exists, the work does not. ⚠️ EVALUATED 2026-08-22: `test/handoff.test.mjs` covers it in four parts — a slice carries its tasks' requirements, criteria and components; a cross-role dependency is visible to the blocked role; no tasks means no slices; and slugs are stable. ⚠️ The cross-role case is covered by a CONSTRUCTED fixture, because this project has exactly one role — so the case the criterion is really about has been tested but not lived.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: For each role in the task graph, the generated slice contains every task assigned to that role together with the requirements and acceptance criteria those tasks trace to, and nothing is a reference to a file outside the package.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every role slice is self-sufficient

acceptanceCriteria.notes: Evaluated 2026-08-22 by test/stage-scope.test.mjs. `stage6Scope` computes the set from `restsOn` on ACTIVE instruction-bearing artifacts, and a name check asserts the module never mentions `loadBearing` (comments stripped first, per the #142 lesson). ⚠️ Falsified: replacing the derivation with a `loadBearing` filter fails four tests, including this criterion's own.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The set of assertions stage 6 checks is computed from `restsOn` on active runbook steps (and any other graph use decided at the time), and contains no reference to the `loadBearing` field.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Stage 6's scope is derived from the graph, not from a flag

acceptanceCriteria.notes: Evaluated 2026-08-22 by test/stage-scope.test.mjs. An assertion whose `loadBearing` is absent OR false is in scope when an active step rests on it — the exact case that passed vacuously (RBS-0001 on AST-0002). ⚠️ CONSTRUCTED, and it had to be: RBS-0001 was retired, so the live graph no longer contains the case its own finding was about.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given a runbook step resting on an assertion whose `loadBearing` is absent or false, that assertion appears in stage 6's evaluated set. This is the exact case that passes vacuously today: RBS-0001 rests on AST-0002, which is unflagged.
acceptanceCriteria.title: An unflagged premise of an active runbook step is in scope

acceptanceCriteria.notes: This is the clause that stops a page-level boundary satisfying DEC-0019 on paper. One boundary wrapping everything makes the whole page the fallback, which technically has a loading state and buys nothing.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The initial HTML of the stage view contains a distinct loading fallback for the exit-criteria region and for the stage-document region. Delaying either read leaves the other region's content rendered and only its own fallback showing.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The stage view's reads resolve behind separate boundaries

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ THE LAST SENTENCE IS THE WHOLE CRITERION. Stripping also produces a page with no executed code, so a test that renders a document and looks for a side effect passes identically on rejection and on silent removal — which is exactly the distinction the amendment to DEC-0020 exists to preserve. The observable being checked is the refusal, not the absence.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: For each of an ESM import, an ESM export, a flow expression, a text expression, a JSX attribute expression, a JSX spread attribute, and a JSX element outside the permitted set: compiling a stage document containing it produces a FAILURE that names the document path and a line:column position. A document that merely renders without the forbidden construct's effect is a FAIL for this criterion.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Each forbidden construct FAILS the compile with a file and position

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The negative criteria above are satisfiable by a compiler that refuses everything. This is the control that stops that.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A stage document containing markdown and only components from the permitted set compiles, renders its markdown structure, and renders each permitted component it uses.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A permitted document renders, including its mapped components

acceptanceCriteria.notes: AST-0030 measured file-routed `@next/mdx` failing exactly this: the document is compiled into the build and an edit changes nothing. That configuration satisfies REQ-0017 and silently fails REQ-0018, which is why this is a criterion rather than an implementation note.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: With the built application serving, editing a stage document on disk changes what the next request for that stage returns, with no rebuild and no restart.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Stage documents compile at request time, not at build time

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ 'Without executing the application' is load-bearing. AST-0022 measured that a non-compliant read is served FRESH whenever a compliant read shares its route, so every behavioural check passes on a codebase that violates the contract until the compliant sibling moves.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A check that runs WITHOUT executing the application reports a failure naming file and line when any module other than the planning-content reader performs a filesystem read rooted at the content directory.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The boundary check fails on a planning-content read outside the reader

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The clause that gets dropped. An abstraction can supply `connection()` while a caller omits the boundary; that builds fine without Cache Components and fails the build with it, so the omission would surface as an unrelated configuration change breaking the build.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The same non-executing check reports a failure when a planning-content read site is not enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary, naming file and line.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The boundary check fails on a read outside a Suspense boundary

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The indirect clause is the bypass path DEC-0021 requires be detected. A direct import is easy to find; a module that re-exports `lib/` and is then imported freely is the same violation wearing one layer.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The same non-executing check reports a failure naming file and line when any module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`, including through a re-export chain that reaches `lib/` indirectly.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The boundary check fails on an app module importing `lib/` directly

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ ADDED BECAUSE IT HAPPENED. A refusal test written during this work passed with the refusal deleted — the assertion that mattered sat behind a condition that was never true. A check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody has seen. This criterion is what makes the three above mean something rather than merely exist.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The check is evaluated against a fixture set containing at least one instance of each violation it claims to detect, and reports a failure for every one. A check that passes the fixture set is a FAIL for this criterion.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The boundary check is itself falsified against known violations

acceptanceCriteria.notes: `export *` would make the adapter a hole rather than a door: the exposed surface would widen every time `lib/` gains an export, including locking and process-spawning modules, with no diff for anyone to review.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every module under `app/server/` has `import 'server-only'` as its first statement and contains no `export *`. Checked statically over the whole directory, with no exemptions.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every adapter module is guarded and explicitly exported

acceptanceCriteria.notes: AST-0033 measured `server-only` throwing outside the RSC compiler. This criterion is what stops the guard migrating into `lib/` later as a tidy-up and breaking the tool to protect the app.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every command under `bin/` and the full test suite run to completion with the shell present, importing `lib/` directly under plain Node with no RSC compiler in play.
acceptanceCriteria.title: `lib/` stays importable under plain Node

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ THE WORDING CLAUSE IS MEASURED, NOT STYLISTIC. Next.js produced two different messages for the same violation reached two ways, and one of them said 'you are using it in the Pages Router' for an App Router project. A test pinned to that string would pass on a wrong message today and break on a corrected one after an upgrade.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A `'use client'` module importing any `app/server/` adapter causes the build to fail with a message naming the offending file and a line:column position. The criterion asserts the presence of a file and a position, and MUST NOT assert the diagnostic's wording.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A client component reaching an adapter fails the build, locatably

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ AST-0036: a line beginning with a colon is ignored by the client parser, so a comment heartbeat keeps the socket warm and fires nothing. The criterion is the listener firing, not bytes arriving, because bytes arriving was never the problem.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: While connected and with no content changing, the stream delivers an event with a name and a data field at least once per configured heartbeat interval, and a client listener registered for that event name fires. A comment-only keepalive is a FAIL for this criterion.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The stream emits a named heartbeat event that page code can observe

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The operator is looking at a browser, not a terminal. A logged failure with a live-looking page is the retained-workspace-reported-destroyed defect in its purest form: the system knows, records it accurately, and tells the person who needs it nothing.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: When the file watcher fails, the page shows the stale indication or the stream closes. A run in which the failure appears only in server output while the page continues to indicate health is a FAIL.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A watcher failure reaches the page, never only a log

acceptanceCriteria.notes: 'Verified by observation, not by the absence of an error' is the tier-1 controller's own rule arriving here: a removal that reports success while the directory survives is retained, and the check has to be `exists()` rather than `!threw`. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: THERE IS NO SECOND PROCESS, AND THERE NEVER WAS ONE TO OWN. This artifact previously said the launcher owns 'both the application process and the file watcher' and 'terminates the watcher with the application'. The watcher is chokidar, imported dynamically INSIDE the `next start` process and held by the change-stream service in that process's memory. A parent launcher cannot call `changeStream.close()` across that boundary without adding IPC or a shutdown endpoint, and neither is justified for a local-first tool. The old wording described a mechanism that could not be built, which is worse than an unmet obligation: it would have been 'satisfied' by a launcher that called nothing and reported success. ⚠️ WHAT IS TRUE INSTEAD, and all of it is enforceable. The launcher owns ONE child: the `next start` process. The change-stream service owns its watcher and closes it when its last subscriber leaves — already built and tested under TSK-0011. Terminating the application process releases any watcher still open through process teardown, which is the operating system's guarantee rather than the launcher's. `close()` stays what it is: a service and test lifecycle operation, never something the launcher claims to call across a process boundary. ⚠️ THIS CRITERION WAS UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AMENDED RATHER THAN REPHRASED. It required that 'no watcher process remains'. There is no watcher process, so the clause could never be observed either true or false — and an unobservable clause in a criterion whose whole point is 'verified by observation, not by the absence of an error' is the exact defect that rule exists to catch, sitting inside the rule. It is amended rather than superseded because it has never been evaluated: no measurement is being retired, and there is no failed outcome to preserve. ⚠️ THE HEARTBEAT PRECONDITION IS PART OF THE CRITERION, not of the test that runs it. The watcher is created lazily on first subscription, so a run that never subscribed would satisfy every remaining clause while having nothing to clean up.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: After the documented launch command is run and then terminated, the child process it started is gone, no process is listening on the application's port, and no temporary directory the launcher created survives — each verified by observation, not by the absence of an error. The run must have opened `/events` and observed a heartbeat before termination, so that a file watcher is known to have existed.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Stopping the launcher leaves nothing behind

acceptanceCriteria.notes: 'No further steps' is the testable half. DEC-0018 fixes the mode: `next build` then `next start`, never the development server. ⚠️ MARKED `pass` IN ERROR ON 2026-08-29 AND RETURNED TO `not-evaluated` THE SAME DAY. EVD-0073 recorded, in its own omissions, that the install branch was never taken: `node_modules` was present in every run, so the launcher printed `dependencies present; skipping install`. This criterion says 'on a machine with... no prior application state' and 'installs and starts'. Half of it was measured and the whole of it was ticked. ⚠️ THE EVIDENCE ITSELF SAID SO, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. The omission was written down accurately and then contradicted by the outcome three lines later — a criterion marked against evidence that explicitly disclaims the thing being claimed. Recording an omission is not the same as honouring it. ⚠️ WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the documented command run in a disposable copy of the repository with no `node_modules` and no `.next`, installing, building, serving and cleaning up with no further steps. ⚠️ EVALUATED PROPERLY 2026-08-29 (EVD-0074) AND RETURNED TO `pass`. The documented command was run in a disposable copy holding only tracked files, with `node_modules` and `.next` confirmed absent. It installed, built, served and cleaned up in 27.2s with no further steps, and the install branch was asserted positively rather than inferred from the run succeeding.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: On a machine with the repository and Node present and no prior application state, the documented command installs and starts the application in production mode, and the project view responds, without further steps.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The application installs and starts from one documented command

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The byte-identical clause is what makes this objective rather than a claim about intent. #82's two-axis split is the reason `lifecycle` is named explicitly: one `status` field would have let this endpoint retire an artifact by accident.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The review action identifies the artifact by id and type and shows its current status. Submitting a change updates only that artifact's `reviewStatus`, through the existing typed write path with its lock and atomic write; the artifact's `lifecycle` and every other artifact on disk are byte-identical afterwards.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A review update changes one artifact's reviewStatus and nothing else

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ IT SUCCEEDS ACC-0020 AND IT IS NOT ACC-0020 WITH A BIGGER NUMBER. The predecessor bounded read-plus-compile at 300 ms and failed, but the measurement showed the failure came from the read. Widening that budget would have hidden a real unknown behind a comfortable ceiling. This one bounds only the cost that was ever in dispute — whether request-time MDX compilation is affordable — and the read it excluded is carried by its own open question, not dropped. ⚠️ 50 ms IS ROUGHLY TWICE THE MEASURED WORST CASE (29.05 ms p95 across six runs), chosen as headroom for document growth rather than as a description of today. A criterion set at the measurement passes by construction and detects nothing. ⚠️ THE VERIFICATION CLAUSE IS INHERITED DELIBERATELY, and it has been falsified: memoising the compiled document makes `bin/bench-compile.mjs` report VOID with a non-zero exit and no timing figures at all. Without it the cheapest way to pass a compile budget is to stop compiling, which would also break DEC-0020's request-time requirement and AST-0030's finding beneath it. ⚠️ EVALUATED `pass` ON EVD-0071, the same six runs that failed the predecessor: compile p95 was 15.41-29.05 ms in every one. The evidence did not change; the question it was asked did.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The 95th-percentile time spent in `compileStageDocument` for the largest stage document is at or below 50 ms. MEASURED SPAN: the compile call alone — from the moment the reader's document is handed to the compiler to the moment a renderable component is returned — EXCLUDING the planning-content read that precedes it, which is a separate cost under a separate question. ENVIRONMENT: the reference host, with its OS, Node version, Next.js version, @mdx-js/mdx version and CPU model recorded alongside the result; no other significant load. DOCUMENT: the largest stage document by byte count at the time of evaluation, named in the result. WARM-UP: 10 requests issued and discarded. SAMPLE: the next 50 consecutive requests, issued one at a time with no concurrency. VERIFICATION: the compile counter must advance by exactly one per measured request. A run in which any measured request did not compile is VOID, not a pass.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Restricted-MDX compilation stays within 50 ms at p95, under ACC-0020's protocol

accepted.statement: Extend the handoff renderer to emit one slice per role, as a query over tasks grouped by `role`, pulling each task's traced requirements and acceptance criteria with it. No slice is authored or maintained.
accepted.title: Generate role slices from the task graph

accepted.notes: ⚠️ IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-22 as `lib/stage-scope.mjs`, evaluated by `test/stage-scope.test.mjs`. ACC-0011 and ACC-0012 both pass, so this task's derived status is `accepted` — nothing here is stored, and deleting the tests would move it back (#96, DEC-0012). ⚠️ The vacuity the finding named has MOVED rather than gone: with RBS-0001 retired the live scope is empty, so stage 6's criterion is again satisfiable with nothing checked. That is now a fact about the plan rather than about an author's attention, which is why it is attested `n/a` with a stated basis rather than `satisfied`.
accepted.statement: Replace `load-bearing-assertions-at-rung`'s reliance on the optional `loadBearing` flag with a scope derived from the graph — at minimum, every assertion referenced by an active runbook step's `restsOn`.
accepted.title: Derive stage 6's scope from graph use rather than a flag

accepted.notes: First because everything else needs somewhere to live. ⚠️ Production mode only (DEC-0018): `next dev` is a contributor workflow and never a shipped configuration, so the launch command must not offer it as an option. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-27 — A DISCARDED ARCHITECTURE HAD LEAKED IN. The original statement configured `@next/mdx`, an absolute remark-plugin path and Turbopack's config-serialisation constraint. All three belong to FILE-ROUTED MDX, which DEC-0020 explicitly rejected: AST-0030 measured that path compiling the document into the build so an edit changes nothing, which fails REQ-0018. ⚠️ HOW IT GOT IN IS WORTH RECORDING. Those settings came from the PROBE that measured the rejected option. The probe's incidental setup was carried into the plan as though it were the design — the measurement was right and the configuration it needed was the losing alternative's. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-27, and one thing was measured rather than chosen. The routes were first placed at `src/app/` to keep the shell clear of `app/server.mjs`, the walking skeleton DEC-0017 preserves. Next.js ignored them: a root `app/` directory takes precedence over `src/app/`, so the build reported `Route (pages)` with only `/404` and none of the authored files appeared. Moving them to `app/` produced `Route (app)` with `○ /`, and the skeleton is left alone as a colocated non-route file — `server.mjs` is not a `page`, `layout` or `route`, and `.mjs` is not in the default `pageExtensions`. ⚠️ A build that SUCCEEDS while rendering nothing you wrote is the failure mode worth remembering here: `✓ Compiled successfully` was printed both times, and only the route table said which files Next.js had actually found. ⚠️ VERIFIED FROM CLEAN: `.next` removed, `npm run shell:build` from scratch, `next start` bound to 127.0.0.1 only (confirmed against the listening socket, not assumed from the flag), HTTP 200 with the expected body, process terminated and the port confirmed free. `npm audit` reports zero vulnerabilities after adding next, react and react-dom. ⚠️ NOT DONE HERE, on purpose: no MDX integration of any kind, no watcher, no launcher that owns processes, and no planning-content read. The route reads nothing — a convenience read would be the first violation of REQ-0021's confinement, whose own enforcement (TSK-0006, TSK-0015) does not exist yet.
accepted.statement: Create the application under `app/` and make `next build` followed by `next start` work on loopback, with a route that responds. No MDX integration of any kind is configured here. The documented one-command launcher is TSK-0013's.
accepted.title: Scaffold the Next.js application and its production build/start primitives

accepted.notes: ⚠️ The review-status write is a LOCKING capability and DEC-0021 holds those back for individual review before exposure — so it is deliberately NOT part of this task. It arrives with the review action, where it can be examined on its own. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-27. Two adapters, a README stating what is deliberately absent, and six static tests — each falsified before being trusted. ⚠️ THE PROBE ROUTES WERE TEMPORARY AND ARE GONE. Verifying that a Server Component can import the adapters needed a route that imports them; verifying the client refusal needed one that violates the rule. Both were built, measured, and deleted, and the tree was rebuilt clean afterwards. Neither reads planning content — REQ-0021 confines reads to the reader, which does not exist until TSK-0005, so even a throwaway route was written to import without reading. ⚠️ `server-only` was added as a dependency. Next.js implements the guard internally and the package's contents are unused, but the specifier must still RESOLVE, so it is a real dependency rather than a documentation flourish.
accepted.statement: Create the adapter modules the shell needs, each beginning with `import 'server-only'` and re-exporting by explicit name or wrapper. Expose only the capabilities the first slice requires. `lib/` itself is not modified and gains no marker, so `bin/` and the test suite keep working under plain Node.
accepted.title: Build the `app/server/*` adapter layer over `lib/`

accepted.notes: ⚠️ Independent boundaries per read region, not one page-level boundary — the latter makes the whole page the fallback and satisfies DEC-0019 on paper while buying nothing. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-27. Five static tests, each falsified: removing a `connection()`, importing `node:fs`, importing `lib/` directly, and adding a synchronous export each turn the suite red. ⚠️ THE ADAPTER GAINED ONE NAME, deliberately and reviewably: `readStageDocs`, taken from the PUBLISHER rather than written fresh. It already owns what a stage document is — `.md` and `.mdx`, dotfiles ignored, anything else REFUSED — and a second reader in the application would have quietly disagreed with the package about which files count. ⚠️ A PREDICTION WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH (AST-0037): the reader was designed expecting bundling to break `toolRoot()`, and it did not. The design is unchanged, for a narrower reason than the original one, and the comment that asserted the wrong thing was corrected.
accepted.statement: Implement the single read path: await `connection()` before each filesystem read, with every read site enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary whose fallback names the content it stands in for. Reads reach `lib/` only through the adapter.
accepted.title: Build the planning-content reader on the `connection()` + Suspense contract

accepted.notes: ⚠️ FOURTH ON PURPOSE, AND THIS IS THE ORDERING DECISION IN THIS PLAN. It could be built last, after there is more to check — and then it would arrive to find a codebase already full of violations, and the pressure would be to weaken the rule rather than fix the code. Built here, it constrains every task after it while the cost of complying is one file at a time. ⚠️ The failing fixtures are not optional polish (ACC-0024): a check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody has seen. ⚠️ SPLIT 2026-08-27. This half needs only the adapter to exist, so it moves earlier and no longer waits on the reader. The read and `<Suspense>` confinement analysis is its sibling. ⚠️ ACC-0024 is satisfied by the PAIR, not by this task alone: both halves must be shown to fail on their own fixtures before the criterion passes. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Three fixtures, eight tests, one lint command, and three defects found before the check was trusted — two by the fixtures (an off-by-one line, and a lazy pattern spanning two statements) and one by running it (a reachability-scoped check that examined almost nothing). ⚠️ A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND IN AN EARLIER TASK'S TEST. ACC-0026's check grepped `lib/` for the string `"server-only"` and went red as soon as a lib module MENTIONED the marker in a comment — which `lib/shell-boundary.mjs` does, since the guard is part of what it explains. It now uses this task's comment-stripping scanner: a check that cannot tell an import from prose is a check that punishes documentation. ⚠️ Fixture adapters deliberately omit `import "server-only"`. Everything under `test/` is collected by `node --test`, and the marker throws outside the RSC compiler (AST-0033), so a fixture carrying it crashed the suite for a reason unrelated to what it tests.
accepted.statement: Implement the analysis that runs without executing the application and reports file and line when any module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`, whether directly or through a re-export chain that reaches `lib/` indirectly. Ship fixtures containing both shapes and prove the check fails on each.
accepted.title: Build the static `app/server` → `lib/` import-boundary check, with failing fixtures

accepted.notes:
⚠️ Request-time compilation, never file-routed `app/**/page.mdx`: AST-0030 measured that path compiling the document into the build, which satisfies REQ-0017 and silently fails REQ-0018. ⚠️ The compiler and plugin chain are PINNED. Changing the MDX version or adding any remark, rehype or recma plugin reopens security validation before it ships. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Twelve tests against a real `@mdx-js/mdx` compile, each rejection asserting a path AND a line:column, plus a control proving an unguarded compile really does evaluate the expression — without which a rejection and a silent strip would be indistinguishable. Falsified three ways: removing the ESM rule, disabling the unmapped-component check, and replacing rejection with stripping each turn the suite red. ⚠️ THE FORMAT DEFAULT WAS THE FINDING (AST-0038), and it was caught by the production probe rather than by the tests — the mapped component rendered as a bare `

`, which led to discovering that a `.md` path disables MDX parsing and with it every rejection. The test fixture is now deliberately named `.md`, so dropping `format: "mdx"` fails nineteen tests. ⚠️ `components.js` is written with `createElement` rather than JSX so that plain Node can import it. A JSX version would have forced the tests to build their own component map, which would have made them a check on a stub rather than on the vocabulary that ships.
accepted.statement: Compile stage documents at request time with `@mdx-js/mdx`, running a remark plugin that FAILS the compile — naming the document path and a line:column — on any ESM import or export, JavaScript expression, JSX attribute expression, JSX spread attribute, or JSX element outside the permitted set. Surface the failure to the operator. Stripping may sit beneath the rejection as defence in depth and may never be the observable behaviour.
accepted.title: Build the restricted MDX compiler with rejection diagnostics

accepted.notes: ⚠️ A comment-line keepalive is ignored by the client parser (AST-0036) — it keeps the socket warm and leaves the page looking healthy. The heartbeat must be an event a listener can fire on. ⚠️ No event buffer, event id or `Last-Event-ID`: events are hints and never deltas, so a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up. ⚠️ Logging a watcher failure to the server console is explicitly not enough. The operator is looking at a browser. ⚠️ SPLIT 2026-08-27 — also named as visibly oversized, and also correctly. The client listener, watchdog, stale state and reload-on-reconnect are its sibling. The split runs along the wire: this task is what is SENT, that one is what is OBSERVED, and AST-0036 is why those are different problems — a comment keepalive is sent and never observed. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Nine deterministic tests plus a production stream check that observes a heartbeat and a change hint from a real file write without waiting for the stream to end. ⚠️ THE BOUNDARY RULE WAS WIDENED DELIBERATELY, AND ONLY WHERE IT WAS WRONG. `only the reader may import app/server/*` was justified by 'or the read escapes connection()' — a justification that covers the CONTENT adapters and nothing else. A change stream watches rather than reads, so the first non-content adapter would have needed an exemption. Instead each adapter now DECLARES its permitted consumers in `shellBoundaryConfig`, defaulting to the reader alone: the same information stated positively, where a reviewer reads it, still failing closed. A test pins the declaration, and asserts the content adapters are not in it. ⚠️ One drift was caught immediately: the read-boundary test listed its options by hand rather than using the shared config, and went red the moment the lint learned about a new consumer — two descriptions of one rule. It now builds from the config.
accepted.statement: Watch the content root and deliver change hints over an event stream. Emit a NAMED heartbeat event carrying data at a fixed interval. When the watcher fails, emit a visible failure signal on the stream or close the stream; logging alone is not permitted.
accepted.title: Build the change-stream server: watcher, transport, named heartbeat, failure propagation

accepted.notes: ⚠️ THIS IS THE INDIVIDUAL REVIEW DEC-0021 REQUIRES, held out of the adapter task for that reason. It is the first locking capability the shell exposes, and a Server Component may run concurrently in ways a CLI never does — that is what needs examining before the line is added. ⚠️ DEPENDENCY CHANGED 2026-08-27: it waited on the change stream, which coupled the first WRITE path to the streaming work for no reason. The review action needs a view to sit in and a URL to identify an artifact by, and nothing else. Review writing and the stream now proceed independently. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-29 (EVD-0072). The first write the application can perform. ⚠️ THREE STANDING PINS MOVED, AND EACH WAS RESTATED RATHER THAN RELAXED. `no adapter exposes a write` now names the one write that was reviewed and keeps refusing every other, including in the same file. The adapter-consumer map gained the write door and an assertion that it admits exactly one caller. And `no synchronous export` in the reader became `no synchronous export that READS`, with the single exception named, its reason recorded, and a check that it is still what it claims — because `planningRoots` is shared with the write so the page and the write cannot address different directories. ⚠️ THAT LAST CHECK WAS INERT WHEN FIRST WRITTEN AND ONLY FALSIFICATION FOUND IT. A `\b` in the generator became a literal backspace byte in the regex, so it matched nothing and passed with a reader that read. It is the same escaping failure this project has now hit several times, and the only reason it did not ship as a decorative rule is that every new check is made to fail before it is believed. ⚠️ THE END-TO-END TEST IS A REAL POST. Next.js renders a hidden action id so a form works without JavaScript, which means the whole path — markup, dispatch, adapter, lock, atomic write, redirect, re-render — is reachable with `fetch`. It asserts the DISK first and the freshly rendered page second, because a write that persisted while the page kept serving the old value would satisfy every other assertion.
accepted.statement: Expose `lib/tools/review-status.mjs` through the adapter and wire the stage view's review panel to it. Updating changes only the named artifact's `reviewStatus`, through the existing lock and atomic write; `lifecycle` and every other artifact are unchanged.

accepted.notes: ⚠️ Deliberately AFTER the change stream, because there is no watcher to own until then. ⚠️ The skeleton's create-on-`listen` / close-in-`close()` pattern does not carry: under `next start` there is no server object the application owns. Choosing the binding is this task's work, and DEC-0022 states the obligation without a mechanism for exactly that reason. ⚠️ Verified by observation, not by the absence of an error — the destroy path's own rule. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-27 to OWN the documented launcher, which TSK-0003 previously claimed. TSK-0003 scaffolds build and start; a launcher that owns two processes cannot exist until there is a watcher to own, so the command is finished here. ACC-0033 stays traced from both — the scaffold is a necessary condition — but this is where it is SATISFIED. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: THERE IS NO SECOND PROCESS, AND THERE NEVER WAS ONE TO OWN. This artifact previously said the launcher owns 'both the application process and the file watcher' and 'terminates the watcher with the application'. The watcher is chokidar, imported dynamically INSIDE the `next start` process and held by the change-stream service in that process's memory. A parent launcher cannot call `changeStream.close()` across that boundary without adding IPC or a shutdown endpoint, and neither is justified for a local-first tool. The old wording described a mechanism that could not be built, which is worse than an unmet obligation: it would have been 'satisfied' by a launcher that called nothing and reported success. ⚠️ WHAT IS TRUE INSTEAD, and all of it is enforceable. The launcher owns ONE child: the `next start` process. The change-stream service owns its watcher and closes it when its last subscriber leaves — already built and tested under TSK-0011. Terminating the application process releases any watcher still open through process teardown, which is the operating system's guarantee rather than the launcher's. `close()` stays what it is: a service and test lifecycle operation, never something the launcher claims to call across a process boundary. ⚠️ THE CLEANUP TEST MUST PROVE THE WATCHER EXISTED FIRST. Without a subscription there is no watcher — the service creates it lazily — so a test that starts the launcher and stops it would observe a clean teardown of nothing and pass vacuously. Opening `/events` and waiting for a named heartbeat is what makes the observation mean something. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-29 (EVD-0073). ⚠️ THE FIRST CLEANUP TEST PASSED AGAINST A LAUNCHER THAT TERMINATED NOTHING, and finding that is most of what this task was worth. Windows reaps the child when the parent exits, so 'the child pid is gone' is true either way; the test now asserts the launcher REPORTED seeing its child exit, which the disabled-termination build fails. ⚠️ A SECOND MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE DESIGN: SIGTERM to the launcher is a hard kill on Windows, so the graceful path never ran and its run directories survived. A stdin stop was added — not for convenience, but because the shutdown guarantee was otherwise unobservable on the platform this project runs on. ⚠️ THE TEST SUITE NEEDED A SHARED LOCK ON `.next`. `node --test` runs files in parallel, and this test and `shell-smoke` both build into and serve from the same directory: first `Another next build process is already running`, then, after a narrow fix that locked only the build, a server dying mid-request because the other test deleted `.next` underneath it. The shared resource was never the build step but the build directory, for as long as anything serves from it. ⚠️ WHAT IS STILL UNEXERCISED: the POSIX shutdown branch (no Linux or macOS host) and a cold install (`node_modules` was present every run).
accepted.statement: Provide the single documented command that installs, builds and starts the application in production mode. It launches Next directly as its owned child rather than through a nested npm process, sets and PRINTS an absolute `PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR`, binds loopback explicitly, forwards shutdown to the child, waits for it to exit, and escalates within a bounded time if it does not. Verify cleanup by observation after termination: the child PID is gone, nothing is listening on the port, and no temporary directory the launcher created survives. The cleanup test must first open `/events` and observe a heartbeat, so that a watcher is known to have existed before anything claims it was released.
accepted.title: Own the documented one-command launcher, and prove its cleanup

accepted.notes: ⚠️ A run in which any measured request did not compile is VOID rather than a pass — the easiest way to hit a compile budget is to cache the document. ⚠️ If the first valid run misses 300 ms by a wide margin, the response is DEC-0020's second alternative — plain markdown for stage documents — not a larger number. That is a PM decision and this task does not take it. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28 (EVD-0071). Six valid runs; ACC-0020 recorded as fail. ⚠️ THIS TASK DOES NOT TAKE THE FALLBACK DECISION, as its own note requires — and the measurement is the reason it should not be taken as written. The budget was missed, but by the read rather than the compiler, so 'plain markdown for stage documents' would cost the rejection contract and buy about 20 ms. That is a PM decision and it now has a different question in front of it: what to do about a per-request read of the whole planning corpus. ⚠️ THE HARNESS IS PERMANENT AND RE-RUNNABLE (`node bin/bench-compile.mjs`), because a number nobody can reproduce is a number nobody can dispute — and this one needs disputing: it is not stable across runs. It prints JSON including every raw sample, so the p95 can be recomputed rather than trusted. ⚠️ IT REFUSES TO REPORT RATHER THAN REPORT SOMETHING FLATTERING. Caching the compiled document produces VOID and a non-zero exit with no timings, falsified by actually memoising it. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-28: the 234-359 ms span was attributed here to reading all 253 artifacts per request. It is not. `readStageDocument` awaits `connection()` and reads the nine stage documents only — `lintProject` is not on its path. What inside that span costs the time is an open question, not a known cost. ⚠️ ACCEPTANCE MOVED 2026-08-28 to ACC-0037, the successor. ACC-0020 stays `fail` and stays readable; this task no longer traces to it, because a task accepted by a retired criterion is accountable to nothing. DEC-0025 records why the plain-Markdown fallback did not fire and QST-0025 carries the unexplained read span.
accepted.statement: Measure the 95th-percentile server-side compile-and-render time for the largest stage document under ACC-0020's protocol: pinned environment recorded with the result, timing from read to completed markup, ten discarded warm-up requests, fifty measured serial requests, and per-request verification that compilation occurred. Record the result as evidence.
accepted.title: Run the compile benchmark under the pinned protocol

accepted.notes: ⚠️ Split from TSK-0006 on 2026-08-27. This half needs the reader to exist, because the rule it enforces is 'reads go through the reader' — there is nothing to be outside of until there is one. ⚠️ ACC-0024 is satisfied by the PAIR with TSK-0006, and it holds for each half separately: a check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody has seen. ⚠️ Both halves land before any view work. Built afterwards they would arrive to a codebase already full of violations, and the pressure would be to weaken the rule rather than fix the code. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Four detectors, six fixtures, eleven tests, and three defects found before anything was trusted — two in the fixtures (import paths that climbed out of the app directory, so the ALLOWED case reported clean because nothing resolved) and one in the analyser (two template-literal regexes that lost a backslash level, leaving a detector unable to fire at all). ⚠️ THE SUSPENSE DETECTORS HAVE NOTHING TO CHECK IN THE REAL APPLICATION YET — the lint reports `0 reader consumer(s)`, because no view imports the reader until TSK-0007. That is stated rather than left for someone to discover: today they are proven by fixtures and by temporary real-code violations, and they begin covering real code with the first view.
accepted.statement: Implement the analysis that runs without executing the application and reports file and line for a planning-content filesystem read performed anywhere other than the reader, and for a read site not enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary. Ship fixtures containing both violations and prove the check fails on each.

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ REQUEST-TIME, NOT BUILD-TIME, AND THAT IS NOT A PERFORMANCE CHOICE. AST-0030 measured that a file-routed `@next/mdx` page is compiled into the build and does not reflect an edit, which REQ-0018 forbids. Routing stage documents as pages would satisfy REQ-0017 and silently fail REQ-0018 while looking correct. ⚠️ OUTSIDE ITS BOUNDARY: it does not read the document (that is the reader) and does not decide the component vocabulary (that is the mapping it is given). ⚠️ IT OWNS DEC-0020's PINNING OBLIGATION: changing the MDX version or adding any remark, rehype or recma plugin reopens security validation before it ships. The rejection was measured at the remark stage only; a later stage could reintroduce what it refused. ⚠️ BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0008. `@mdx-js/mdx` pinned at 3.1.1 exactly, one remark plugin, no rehype or recma stage, compiled at request time. ACC-0017 and ACC-0019 pass. ACC-0018 stays `not-evaluated` because it also evaluates CMP-0016, which does not exist until TSK-0009 — the mapped component IS proven to render, by test and in production, but the criterion covers a pair. ⚠️ `format: "mdx"` IS PART OF THE CONTRACT, and AST-0038 is why. Left to infer the format from the path, the compiler parses a `.md` document as plain markdown: components render as bare paragraphs and expressions compile with NO REJECTION, because the parser produces no nodes for the plugin to refuse. The contract goes vacuous, silently, decided by a filename — and it had already made a test pass on all nine real stage documents for the wrong reason. ⚠️ REJECTION IS THE CONTRACT AND STRIPPING SITS UNDERNEATH IT. A test in the suite proves the difference is observable: with the plugin removed the same document compiles and its expression EVALUATES, so a check that only looked for an absent side effect could not tell a refusal from a silent removal. ⚠️ THE DIAGNOSTIC DOES NOT REACH THE BROWSER ON ITS OWN (AST-0039): a refusal surfaces as a 200 and an opaque digest. Catching `StageDocumentRejected` and rendering its path and position is the stage view's obligation.
components.responsibility: Compile a stage document to a renderable component at request time using `@mdx-js/mdx`, running the rejection plugin that fails the compile with a file path and a line:column position on any ESM import or export, JavaScript expression, JSX attribute expression, JSX spread attribute, or JSX element outside the permitted component set. Own the pinned compiler and plugin chain.

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ THE GUARD CANNOT LIVE IN `lib/`, which is why this component exists rather than a one-line edit. AST-0033 measured that `server-only` throws when imported outside the RSC compiler, and `lib/` is imported by every `bin/` command and the whole test suite — marking it would guard the application by breaking the tool. ⚠️ IT PREVENTS NOTHING THE BUILD DID NOT ALREADY PREVENT. Both client-import cases already fail; what the marker buys is a LOCATABLE failure. Unguarded, Turbopack reports an internal error with `location: undefined` and no filename (AST-0032). ⚠️ OUTSIDE ITS BOUNDARY: it holds no logic of its own. A wrapper that adapts a signature is permitted; a wrapper that decides anything belongs in `lib/`, where the tool and the app share it. ⚠️ BUILT 2026-08-27 BY TSK-0004, and all three of its criteria now PASS — the first component of the shell to be accepted rather than merely coded. `implementedBy` says code exists; ACC-0025, ACC-0026 and ACC-0027 passing is what says it works, and the two statements are separate on purpose (QST-0015). ⚠️ THE SURFACE IS TWO MODULES AND IT IS DELIBERATELY SMALL: content-root resolution, the lint context builders, `lintProject`, stage definitions, `loadStageAttestations` and `evaluateStageGate`. Nothing that locks, writes, spawns or holds state. `evaluateHandoffGate` is absent too — publication readiness is not something a view needs to compute. ⚠️ THE CASE THAT JUSTIFIES THE NO-WILDCARD RULE IS REAL AND IS IN THIS DIRECTORY. `loadStageAttestations` and `writeStageAttestation` are exports of the SAME module, and only the first is a read. `export * from "../../lib/attestations.mjs"` would have exposed a lock-taking capability silently, on a line nobody would have read twice. A test now forbids that export by name.
components.responsibility: Be the only door from application code into `lib/`. Each module begins with `import 'server-only'`, re-exports by explicit name or wrapper rather than `export *`, and exposes only the capabilities the shell needs; process-spawning, locking and stateful modules pass through individual review before they are exposed at all.

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ THE HEARTBEAT IS A NAMED EVENT, NOT A COMMENT, and that correction came from AST-0036. A comment line is ignored by the client parser, so a comment keepalive fixes the bytes and not the visibility — the one consumer that needs to see it is the only one specified to ignore it. The skeleton's idle and dead streams are byte-identical (AST-0034), which is what REQ-0018's second clause forbids. ⚠️ RECONNECTION IS ITSELF A CHANGE HINT. Because events are hints and never deltas (#73), a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up — so no event buffer, no `id:` field and no `Last-Event-ID` handling are needed. This is the one place in the design where the contract removes work rather than adding it. ⚠️ A WATCHER FAILURE EMITS A VISIBLE SIGNAL OR CLOSES THE STREAM. Logging alone is forbidden: the operator is looking at a browser, and a logged failure with a live-looking page is the retained-workspace-reported-destroyed defect exactly. ⚠️ SERVER HALF BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0011. ACC-0028 and ACC-0031 pass. ACC-0029 (a stopped heartbeat produces a visibly stale page) and ACC-0030 (reconnect reloads and recovers a missed change) stay `not-evaluated` — they are about the CLIENT, and TSK-0017 owns it. ⚠️ IT IS A SERVICE, NOT AN IMPORT-TIME SIDE EFFECT. Nothing starts until the first subscription, chokidar is imported dynamically inside the factory, and `close()` is explicit so the service and its tests can end it deterministically. `next build` imports every route module to collect page data, and a watcher started at import would run during the build and outlive it. ⚠️ THE WATCHER IS SHARED AND THE SUBSCRIBERS ARE NOT. One tab closing clears its own timer and leaves every other page refreshing; the watcher closes when the last subscriber leaves. ⚠️ A FAILURE IS BROADCAST THEN THE STREAMS CLOSE, so a client can tell a dead watcher from a dropped connection. Logging alone would leave every open page looking healthy while nothing could ever refresh it — DEC-0022's rule, and the reason this is an event rather than a console line. ⚠️ CLIENT HALF BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0017 (EVD-0070). ACC-0029 and ACC-0030 STAY `not-evaluated`: no browser was available, and both are about what a page does, not about what the logic would do. The logic behind them is tested; the behaviour is not observed, and marking them would claim a measurement nobody took. ⚠️ IT IS THE APPLICATION'S ONLY CLIENT COMPONENT, and it holds nothing a reload would lose — DEC-0023's rule as corrected. `location.reload()` rather than an assignment, so the URL and with it both selections survive every refresh this component causes. ⚠️ STATE IS TEXT FIRST, icon second, colour last. AST-0034 measured an idle stream and a dead one as byte-identical: this indicator is the only thing between the operator and a page that looks fine while nothing can refresh it, so it must not depend on colour to be read. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: an earlier note here said `close()` was 'explicit for TSK-0013's launcher to own'. It is not and cannot be — the launcher is a parent process and this service is an in-process singleton inside its child. `close()` is a SERVICE AND TEST lifecycle operation: the service calls it when its last subscriber leaves, and tests call it to end a stream deterministically. What the launcher contributes is terminating the child, after which process teardown releases anything still open. ⚠️ ACC-0029 AND ACC-0030 EVALUATED 2026-08-29 IN A REAL BROWSER (EVD-0075); both pass, and the first run of that evaluation FAILED and found a defect that made this component inert in every shipped page. `timers = { setTimeout, clearTimeout }` throws `Illegal invocation` in a browser (AST-0040); the watchdog never armed, and the indicator reported a healthy stream forever. Thirteen unit tests passed throughout, because every one of them injected timers and none called the default. ⚠️ `test/stream-watchdog.test.mjs` NOW CALLS THE DEFAULT with `globalThis.setTimeout` wrapped in the same brand check a browser applies, so the defect is catchable in Node from now on. It was falsified against the original code before being trusted.
components.responsibility: Keep every open view current: watch the content root, emit a named heartbeat event carrying data at a fixed interval, deliver change notifications as hints, and run the client watchdog that renders a visibly disconnected state when a heartbeat does not arrive. On reconnection, reload.
components.title: Change stream

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ IT IS THE FIRST LOCKING CAPABILITY THE ADAPTER MUST EXPOSE, and DEC-0021 holds locking modules back for individual review precisely so this one is examined rather than arriving as a line in an adapter. A Server Component may run concurrently in ways a CLI never does. ⚠️ `reviewStatus` ONLY. #82's two-axis split is doing work here: review progress is the application's to change and `lifecycle` is not, and a single `status` field would have let this endpoint retire an artifact by accident. ⚠️ OUTSIDE ITS BOUNDARY: it does not decide whether a status change is allowed — the typed tool owns that, and one implementation serves both the CLI and the app (#47). ⚠️ BUILT 2026-08-29 BY TSK-0012 (EVD-0072), after the individual review DEC-0021 requires. ACC-0034 passes. ⚠️ IT REUSES `lib/tools/review-status.mjs` RATHER THAN REIMPLEMENTING IT, which is the whole of why this could be approved: the lock, the fresh read inside the lock and the atomic write are the ones the CLI already used, so there is no second copy to drift. ⚠️ THE ADAPTER EXPOSES ONE WRITE AND ADMITS ONE CALLER. `app/server/review.js` re-exports `setReviewStatus` and nothing else that writes, and `shellBoundaryConfig` names the Server Action as its only permitted consumer. Both are pinned by tests that fail by name when a second write or a second caller appears — a second caller being a second place the content lock can be taken from, which is the review needing to happen again. ⚠️ THE HARD PART IS IN A MODULE WITH NO `server-only`, for the reason CMP-0017's client half is: everything decidable about a write — refusals before the lock is taken, a bad status never reaching disk, what two concurrent submissions leave behind — is reachable only from plain Node, and concurrency is what a browser test is worst at provoking on purpose.
components.responsibility: Perform review-status changes from the application through the existing typed write path — lock, fresh read inside the lock, atomic write — reusing `lib/tools/review-status.mjs` rather than reimplementing it, and reaching it through the server adapter layer.

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ IT EXISTS BECAUSE TESTING CANNOT DO THIS. AST-0022 measured that a non-compliant read is served FRESH whenever a compliant read shares its route, so every behavioural freshness check passes on a codebase that breaks the contract — until the compliant sibling moves, and then every read on that route silently reverts to build-time content. A test that passes on broken code is worse than no test, because it is also a claim that the code was checked. ⚠️ TWO EDGES, ONE GRAPH: reads outside the abstraction, and `app/**` importing `lib/**` outside `app/server/`. The adapter boundary has the same property — an app module importing `lib/` directly behaves identically until someone renders it from a client component. ⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS NOT FIXED HERE: a lint rule, a module-boundary constraint, a generated accessor or a build-step scan would each satisfy it. What is fixed is that it runs without executing the application. ⚠️ HALF BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0006. The `app/server` → `lib/` import boundary is analysed, falsified and wired into `npm run lint:shell` and the test suite. ACC-0023 passes. ⚠️ ACC-0021, ACC-0022 AND ACC-0024 REMAIN `not-evaluated`. The planning-read and `<Suspense>` confinement half is TSK-0015, and ACC-0024 asks for the FULL violation set with failing fixtures — marking it now would claim a pair on the strength of one half. ⚠️ SCOPE IS EVERY MODULE UNDER `app/`, NOT ONLY WHAT A ROUTE REACHES, and that was a corrected defect rather than an initial choice. Reachability-scoped, the check walked two files and reported the project clean while never looking at the reader or either adapter. Reachability now supplies only the chain that explains a violation. ⚠️ ONE EXCLUSION, DECLARED IN `shellBoundaryConfig`: `app/server.mjs`, the walking skeleton DEC-0017 preserves. Excluding it by name makes a second exclusion a visible act; excluding it by unreachability would have silently excluded most of the shell. ⚠️ COMPLETED 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0015. All four of its criteria now pass. Both halves run from one command, `npm run lint:shell`, and from the test suite. ⚠️ SIX DETECTORS ACROSS THE TWO HALVES, EACH WITH A FIXTURE THAT FIRES IT, and a test that counts them — so a detector added later without a control fails the suite rather than joining it quietly. Each of those would have produced a green result from a check that examined nothing. ⚠️ WHAT IT CANNOT SEE, recorded rather than implied: a computed specifier; a component rendered through a variable or passed as a prop rather than by name; and a path alias, since only relative specifiers are resolved and none is configured today.
components.responsibility: Statically prove, without executing the application, that every planning-content read goes through the reader inside a `<Suspense>` boundary and that no module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`. Detect bypass paths rather than only direct violations.
components.title: Import-boundary check

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ PRODUCTION MODE ONLY (DEC-0018): `next build` then `next start`. `next dev` is a contributor workflow and is not a shipped configuration — AST-0015 showed the two produce different artifacts, so shipping the development server would mean shipping something this project can never validate. ⚠️ THE PROCESS OWNERSHIP IS AN OBLIGATION WITH NO MECHANISM YET, deliberately. The skeleton creates its watcher on `listen` and closes it in its own `close()`, but that belongs to a process owning its own HTTP server; under `next start` there is no such object and nothing has been run. Choosing and validating the binding is this component's design work. ⚠️ PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-27 BY TSK-0003, and `implementedBy` now points at the scaffold. Read it as exactly what QST-0015's answer says it means — CODE EXISTS — and nothing more. What exists is the Next.js application, a production build, a loopback start script and one route that responds. What does NOT exist is the thing this component is mostly about: a launcher that owns both the application process and the file watcher and terminates the watcher with it. There is no watcher yet to own. ⚠️ BOTH ITS CRITERIA REMAIN `not-evaluated`, deliberately. ACC-0033 (installs and starts from one documented command) is not satisfied by two scripts a reader has to compose themselves, and ACC-0032 (stopping the launcher leaves nothing behind) has nothing to stop. TSK-0013 finishes both. This is the state the planned/built axis was rejected for being unable to express: a populated `implementedBy` beside unevaluated criteria says 'some code, unjudged' precisely, where a boolean would have had to lie in one direction or the other. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: THERE IS NO SECOND PROCESS, AND THERE NEVER WAS ONE TO OWN. This artifact previously said the launcher owns 'both the application process and the file watcher' and 'terminates the watcher with the application'. The watcher is chokidar, imported dynamically INSIDE the `next start` process and held by the change-stream service in that process's memory. A parent launcher cannot call `changeStream.close()` across that boundary without adding IPC or a shutdown endpoint, and neither is justified for a local-first tool. The old wording described a mechanism that could not be built, which is worse than an unmet obligation: it would have been 'satisfied' by a launcher that called nothing and reported success. ⚠️ WHAT IS TRUE INSTEAD, and all of it is enforceable. The launcher owns ONE child: the `next start` process. The change-stream service owns its watcher and closes it when its last subscriber leaves — already built and tested under TSK-0011. Terminating the application process releases any watcher still open through process teardown, which is the operating system's guarantee rather than the launcher's. `close()` stays what it is: a service and test lifecycle operation, never something the launcher claims to call across a process boundary. ⚠️ THIS COMPONENT'S DESIGN WORK SHRANK RATHER THAN GREW. Its notes called 'choosing and validating the binding' the substance of the component; there is no binding to choose. What is left is a real and checkable job: one command, an absolute content root printed at startup, loopback bound explicitly, shutdown forwarded, the child waited for, and a bounded escalation if it does not go. ⚠️ BUILT 2026-08-29 BY TSK-0013 (EVD-0073). ACC-0032 and ACC-0033 pass. ⚠️ IT OWNS ONE CHILD AND SAYS SO. `next start` is spawned directly with Node, so the pid it holds IS the server's — through `npm run` it would hold a shim, and on Windows a `.cmd` shim whose child does not reliably receive a forwarded signal. ⚠️ THE CONTENT ROOT IS ABSOLUTE AND PRINTED, and a missing one is exit code 2 rather than a fallback. The application would otherwise resolve to its own directory and be correct with no way for the operator to know WHICH directory — #70's refusal-to-guess at the launcher. ⚠️ ITS RUN DIRECTORY EXISTS PARTLY SO CLEANUP CAN BE OBSERVED. It carries the run record a supervisor reads to find the child; its removal is one of ACC-0032's three observations, and a launcher with no temporary state would make that clause vacuous. ⚠️ ACC-0033 RE-EVALUATED 2026-08-29 (EVD-0074) after being marked `pass` on evidence that disclaimed the install branch. It now rests on a cold run: no `node_modules`, no `.next`, install branch taken and asserted, content root verified to be inside the copy rather than the source repository.
components.responsibility: Install and run the shell from one documented command: build the application and start it in production mode, owning the `next start` process as a child, forwarding shutdown to it, waiting for it to exit, and leaving nothing behind — no process on the port, no temporary directory it created. The file watcher is an in-process resource of the child and is released by its teardown.
components.title: Launcher

note: Generated as a query over the task graph, grouped by `task.role` (#19). Nothing here is authored: re-running the handoff recomputes it, so a slice cannot drift from the plan. `tasks` is work REMAINING; `accepted` is work already finished, listed so nobody repeats it. Both statuses are derived from acceptance criteria, never stored.

requirements.rationale: Intake: 'the runbook should represent the output of discovery, not the beginning of discovery.'
requirements.statement: No instruction in the final output may rest on a claim whose basis is below the level required for that instruction.
requirements.title: Instructions rest on resolved claims

requirements.rationale: Intake objective, stated in the PM's own terms.
requirements.statement: A recipient of the output must be able to begin their part of the work without asking the planner for information the plan should have contained.
requirements.title: The handoff is actionable without returning to the planner

requirements.rationale: Intake stakeholders: the material explicitly declines to assume which the implementer is. This is testable by comparing both consumers against the same required-information inventory.
requirements.statement: For every required item in the handoff, both a human reader and an automated consumer must be able to recover the same information without depending on the other representation.
requirements.title: The output serves a human or an agent implementer

requirements.rationale: REQ-0002 requires current project state to be inspectable at any time, and stage position is the coarsest form of that state. Deriving it rather than storing it follows #16: stage status is derived from artifacts, never persisted alongside them.
requirements.statement: The application shows which stage the project is in, derived from the stage definitions and the recorded attestations rather than from a stored status value.
requirements.title: The application displays the project's current stage

requirements.rationale: Stage documents are the narrative half of the plan and are agent-authored. Rendering them is the point of choosing MDX; bounding what they may execute is what keeps content from becoming application code.
requirements.statement: The application renders the MDX stage document for a selected stage, and a document referencing a component outside the permitted set does not execute arbitrary code.
requirements.title: The application renders a stage document authored in MDX

requirements.rationale: The agent and the operator write the same files (#15), so a view that only refreshes on reload shows state that has already moved. The second clause is the harder half: a silently dead stream renders stale content that looks live.
requirements.statement: When a file under the content root is changed by something other than the application, the application's view updates without the operator reloading the page, and a dropped update stream is visibly distinguishable from an idle one.
requirements.title: The application reflects external content changes without a manual reload

requirements.rationale: #88 forbids authoring content by any route but a typed operation, and #78 plus #72 make the write safe against the agent writing concurrently. A second write path in the app would be a second protocol against the same files.
requirements.statement: A review-status change made in the application is written by the existing typed operation — lock, fresh read inside the lock, atomic write — and the application contains no other write path into content.
requirements.title: The application performs review-status updates through the existing typed write path

requirements.rationale: The product is a local-first tool a consumer clones (#1, #20, #32). An application whose supported mode is undeclared cannot be validated against the configuration it actually ships in — which is why AST-0010 is deferred rather than answered.
requirements.statement: An operator can install and start the application on a clean machine from documented commands, and the supported deployment mode is stated rather than implied.
requirements.title: The application is installable and runnable locally from a documented command

requirements.notes: ⚠️ THIS IS AN ARCHITECTURAL REQUIREMENT, NOT A TESTING PREFERENCE, and the distinction is what AST-0022 establishes. 'Verify it behaves correctly' is unavailable here as a matter of measured fact rather than of rigour — the observable behaviour of a compliant and a non-compliant read is IDENTICAL on a route that has at least one compliant read. The property has to be enforced where it is visible, which is in the source. ⚠️ TWO OBLIGATIONS, and the second is the one that gets forgotten: confine the read, AND check the boundary. DEC-0019 requires both `connection()` before the read and a `<Suspense>` boundary around it, and an abstraction can supply the first while a caller omits the second. A check that only looks for stray `readFileSync` calls would pass an application whose every read is correctly routed and unboundaried — which builds fine without Cache Components and FAILS THE BUILD with it, so the omission surfaces as a configuration change breaking the build rather than as the contract violation it is. ⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS DELIBERATELY UNSPECIFIED. A lint rule, a module-boundary constraint, a generated single accessor, or a build step that greps for content-root paths would each satisfy this; choosing among them is stage 5 design work that belongs with the components, and naming one here would decide it before the components exist. What is fixed is the PROPERTY: checkable without executing the application. ⚠️ IT INTERACTS WITH QST-0018 AND DOES NOT PRE-EMPT IT. If a stage document may reference components, then the permitted-component set is also a surface through which a direct read could enter, and static confinement has to cover it. That is a constraint QST-0018's answer must satisfy, not a decision about what that answer is. ⚠️ IT DOES NOT SETTLE CACHE COMPONENTS. DEC-0019 was chosen precisely so the contract holds with that flag either way, and a static check on source has nothing to say about it. Any enforcement design that only works under one setting would spend the property DEC-0019 bought. ⚠️ SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-08-27 BY DEC-0021: the same static check must also enforce that no application module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`, and must detect bypass paths. It is one more forbidden edge in the same import graph, not a second mechanism — and it is the same failure shape as AST-0022, because the adapter boundary is a convention that nothing observable distinguishes from a violation: an app module importing `lib/` directly behaves identically until someone renders it from a client component.
requirements.rationale: AST-0022 measured that a read violating the contract is served FRESH whenever a compliant read shares its route — the compliant read makes the route dynamic and the violation rides along. So a behavioural check cannot see the violation: every freshness test passes on a codebase that breaks the contract, right up until the compliant sibling is moved, cached or deleted, at which point every read on that route silently reverts to build-time content. A test that passes on broken code is worse than no test, because it is also a claim that the code was checked.
requirements.statement: Every read of planning content in the application goes through a single reading abstraction that applies the DEC-0019 contract. A direct filesystem read of the content root anywhere else in the application fails a check that does not depend on running the application or observing what it serves, and the same check verifies that each read site is enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary. Acceptance for REQ-0016, REQ-0017 and REQ-0018 may not rest on freshness behaviour alone.
requirements.title: Planning-content reads are confined to the approved abstraction, and the confinement is checked statically
